objective: Exercise read-only visible-label discovery across four cameras and two separated frames from Capture_20261103, while retaining request-level latency evidence and strict truth isolation.

benchmark.source: Capture_20261103 cameras 0-3, first and last selected frame
benchmark.raw_artifact_note: The raw artifact was written before the even-sized median implementation was corrected and therefore contains the upper-middle value 24350.0. The immutable run rows recompute to the exact median 24336.5; the benchmark code and regression test now use the exact definition.

visual_review.review_type: assistant visible-content review, not human annotation truth
notes: The camera-0 first frame visibly contains a ramp, floor, foreground ego platform/person and other robots; the reported major categories are supported.
Camera-1 frames visibly contain pallets, people, floor and ego structure; the reported categories are supported.
Camera-2 frames visibly contain people, floor, ego structure, pallets in the first frame and another forklift in the last frame; the reported categories are supported.
Camera-3 last frame visibly contains a loaded pallet, floor, ego structure and another forklift; the reported categories are supported.

Camera-0 last and camera-3 first report both generic vehicle and other_robot. The visible forklift may be the same physical object under two labels, so this is retained as a semantic overcall risk rather than accepted as truth.
visual_review.slope_limit: The exercise confirms that a visible ramp can be named in one camera view. It does not measure slope mask IoU, boundary quality or traversable-area union quality.

boundaries: Eight successful service requests prove bounded runtime compatibility, not eight correct annotations.
There is no independent per-view human category truth in this benchmark.
No model, prompt, schema, candidate, truth or training behavior changed in this round.
The generic-vehicle versus other-robot overlap remains an observed generalization risk for a later truth-backed gate.
